head: f05d6f9d591184b3884754f76dcee49cd9e8f82f
scope: Issue 207. A foreground lane router on port 18797 ran this code on Linux 7.0 x86_64, beside the daily router, with its state on the machine's ext4 disk. It ran in a user and network namespace (lane.py). The namespace's /etc/hosts sent api.anthropic.com and raw.githubusercontent.com through socat bridges to the real hosts, and platform.claude.com to token_endpoint.py, a controlled token endpoint. Real accounts: copies of the severus and real-5 logins, whose tokens expired more than 4.5 h later, read paid overflow and usage and served requests through the real API. real-5 was the only daily login with weekly capacity left, so it answered the test messages, and two logins keep the lane's usage reads low beside the daily router's reads of the same accounts. The record labels the one daily login that no earlier record names as real-5; the lane's evidence names it. Controlled: the fake logins expired and flaky, whose refresh tokens the controlled endpoint answered with 400 invalid_grant "Refresh token expired" and with 503. No real refresh token could reach the real token endpoint, and none reached the controlled one. The router marked expired as needing login at start, and status and claude-router status showed it with its login step. claude_router.py check warned with the login step and passed, before and after a restart, and its test messages went only to real accounts. A 503 left flaky signed in, and check failed on its missing reading as before. tests/test_claude_router_activate.py covers the update path, which runs the same check. record.py built the record. Unchanged historical scenarios are references and were not rerun.

matrix.scenario: The lane copies only chosen daily logins whose tokens expire more than 4.5 h from now, outside the four-hour refresh lead
Lane code, executable, and SDK match the build at f05d6f9 and go.mod
severus and real-5 are signed in with paid overflow disabled at start
At least one real account has weekly capacity for the test messages
The token endpoint refused expired's refresh token, and the router marked expired as needing login at start

detail.method: lane.py ran the router in a user and network namespace whose /etc/hosts (lane-hosts) sent platform.claude.com to token_endpoint.py on 127.0.0.1:443, with a certificate that a lane CA signed and SSL_CERT_FILE trusted. The SDK's own refresh of the fake expired login, due at start, got 400 with the body the Mac mini's service.log recorded. The router marked expired before it began listening.

matrix.scenario: expired's read fails at once with the refusal and sends no usage request

detail.last_read_failure: the token endpoint refused the credential's refresh token; the account needs login
reads: the token endpoint refused the credential's refresh token; the account needs login

An update's recheck calls the same run_check.

matrix.scenario: Identity is the same at the start and the end
Paid overflow remains disabled on the real accounts
The daily router kept running in the same process during the lane run
No real refresh token was exchanged or changed, and none reached the token endpoint

detail.method: Real refresh tokens could not reach the real token endpoint: the namespace resolved platform.claude.com to the controlled endpoint, which logs SHA-256 prefixes. Its log holds only the two fake tokens. lane.py hashed each real refresh token in the daily login before it copied it, and again in the lane's copy after the last stop.

Exact client token, the tokens in the lane's login copies and fake logins, plus sk-ant-, JWT, Bearer, and lane fake-token patterns, before the copies were deleted. lane.py and token_endpoint.py hold only the patterns.

incidents.finding: The SDK's refresh of the fake expired login ended before the router registered its refresh guard. The guard recorded the refresh token as failed but not refused, so the start read failed with the generic failure text, and the router marked expired only at the SDK's retry a minute later. Separately, dobby and work, the only real accounts in that run, had exhausted their weekly windows, so the check's test message got 429 on both.
incidents.fixed_in: refreshguard.go: a credential whose SDK failure record already holds a refusal when the guard is registered has its refresh token recorded as refused, so the start read marks the account (TestRefusalOfAnSDKRefreshThatBeganBeforeTheGuardMarksTheAccountAsNeedingLogin, refused before the guard is registered). lane.py copies every daily login outside its refresh lead.

incidents.result: stopped before any message: personal, dobby, and work had no weekly capacity
incidents.finding: lane.py's capacity check stopped the run before it sent a message.
incidents.fixed_in: lane.py copies every daily login outside its refresh lead, which added severus and real-5.

incidents.finding: Review renamed and merged the read path's refusal helpers and deleted comments, which changed the router code digest without changing behavior.
incidents.fixed_in: The fourth run's rows replaced the third run's.

incidents.finding: An outside Correctness review found two defects that no lane row exercised. A settings read that succeeded after a refusal cleared the mark through login confirmation, and a 503 whose body quoted a 400 invalid_grant counted as a refusal.
incidents.fixed_in: internal/router persists refresh_refused, which keeps login confirmation from clearing a refusal's mark (TestASettingsReadThatSucceedsAfterARefusalKeepsTheAccountNeedingLogin). The classifier reads the SDK's own status, the leftmost in its error text (TestOnlyARefusedRefreshTokenMarksTheAccountAsNeedingLogin).

incidents.finding: In the flaky phase the usage endpoint answered 429 to every real account's reads, with Retry-After up to 5 minutes. Three runs in 20 minutes had read six real accounts three times each, beside the daily router's own reads, so check failed on the real accounts' missing readings and their paid overflow was unread at the end. The refusal rows passed. Review fixes after this run renamed RequireLogin to RefreshRefused and changed its doc comment, which changed the router code digest.
incidents.fixed_in: lane.py copies only two real logins. The sixth run started after the rate limit's Retry-After had passed. Its rows replaced the fifth run's.

prior_acceptance.status: historical reference, not rerun at this code
